what: The page is drawn with blur 30px and opacity .8, then right after attaching only the blur clears over 1s easeOutSine(0.39,0.575,0.565,1) (opacity goes straight to 1) — clicking a same-site link starts blur and opacity again at the same length and navigates right away, so the next page resolves out of the blur. Returning with Back is clear again

options.go: Time from press to navigating (sec), default 0 (the original setTimeout has no delay) — give it .5 and the spread is visible before navigating

note: While a filter is on body (the first 1s), position: fixed elements inside are drawn relative to body — the original is the same. If the motion part script can’t run the page stays blurred, so be sure to load it together.

from.where: Every page’s body (original script.js: body.fade-in on DOMContentLoaded — body{filter: blur(30px); opacity: .8; transition: 1s all var(--easeOutSine)} .fade-in{filter: none; opacity: 1; transition: 1s filter} · On link click, remove fade-in and navigate with setTimeout(0))
